name: Garrafina
description: Garrafina is a Spanish train domino game in which each player extends a personal train from a central starting double. Trains become open to opponents when their owner passes, creating a tactical open or private state on every branch.

overview.description: Garrafina is a Spanish train domino game in which each player extends a personal train from a central starting double. Trains become open to opponents when their owner passes, creating a tactical open or private state on every branch.

history.origins: Garrafina developed in Spanish domino circles as a trains-family game related to Mexican Train but with stricter ownership rules for each player's branch.
timeline: 20th century: Popularized in Spanish social domino play.
2000s onward: Online platforms such as Ludoteka helped standardize three- and four-player procedures.
history.cultural: Garrafina is common in Spanish-language domino communities and often played as a multi-deal score session.
history.evolution: Core play remained stable while table rules varied on session length, tie handling in blocked hands, and two- or three-player exchange procedures.

setup.players: 2 to 4 players; four-player is the base form.
setup.deck: One double-six domino set of 28 tiles.
setup.dealing: Deal 7 tiles to each player. In 4-player games all tiles are dealt. In 3-player games one 7-tile heap remains face down. In 2-player games two 7-tile heaps remain face down.
setup.equipment: Optional train markers to show which trains are open after a pass.

rules.objective: Play all tiles first, or in a blocked hand have the lowest pip total on unplayed tiles.
rules.gameplay: In the first deal, the holder of highest double leads it as the center. In later deals, the designated starting player may lead any double; if none, they pass and turn continues until someone leads a double. Each player has a personal train extending from the center. On turn, a player must play if legal. A legal play is usually to own train, but a player may instead play to another player's train only if that owner previously passed and the end has not changed since that pass. When a player passes, their train is open. If another player adds a non-double to that open train, it becomes private again. Play ends when a player empties hand or everyone is blocked.
keyRules: If a legal tile exists on any currently legal train, passing is not allowed.
Open-train status is tied to pass state and can close again when its end changes.
In blocked hands, lowest pip total wins; if two or more tie for least spots, there is no winner and no one scores.
Session end is by agreed deal count or agreed target score.

strategy.basic: Keep your train playable to avoid opening it to opponents.
strategy.intermediate: Use opponents' open trains to unload awkward tiles while preserving your own control numbers.
strategy.advanced: Track who can likely answer each branch end; selectively close an opponent train by changing its end after they pass.
tips: In four-player games all 28 tiles are in hands, so memory of seen numbers is highly valuable.
Plan around doubles because they preserve branch direction and can stabilize your own train timing.

variations.name: Three-Player Heap Exchange
variations.description: With three players, one face-down 7-tile heap may be exchanged for a player's original hand under first-turn conditions; at most one exchange per deal.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes heap count and exchange rules; no engine constant overrides documented in source.

variations.name: Two-Player Double Heap
variations.description: With two players there are two 7-tile heaps; exchange may happen twice. If the loser exchanged twice, loss can be multiplied accordingly.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes heap count and loss multiplier; no engine constant overrides documented in source.

variations.name: Correlativa
variations.description: Mexican variant without full-hand exchange. Unplayed tiles stay in boneyard; blocked players draw one by one until playable or boneyard empty.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant adds boneyard and draw mechanic; no engine constant overrides documented in source.

scoring.description: When someone goes out, each loser loses points equal to pips left in hand and winner gains their sum. In blocked hands, each loser loses the difference between their pips and the winner's pips; winner gains sum of losses.
scoring.winCondition: Win each deal by going out first or having the lowest pip total when blocked; win session by agreed deal count or reaching agreed target.

synthesis.shortDescription: Spanish train domino game where passing opens your branch for opponents and blocked hands score by pip difference.
